pumpkin-curly-vine.heading: Leave space for the vine
pumpkin-curly-vine.use: The broad pumpkin body works as a focal point on an autumn worksheet or a personal greeting card. The vine reaches to the upper right, so place a caption below the drawing or to its left instead of pushing text against the curl. Keep the stem and leaf visible when cropping; they help the silhouette read as a pumpkin rather than an orange circle.
pumpkin-curly-vine.edit: Select Pumpkin skin to change the body first. The rib shadows and highlights are separate surfaces, so a large hue change may need corresponding adjustments to those layers. For a simpler coloring activity, compare the outline preset with a version that hides fine decorative accents.
pumpkin-curly-vine.check: The thin vine is the first detail to check on a small print. Avoid stretching the image sideways to fill a label; retain the square canvas ratio or crop deliberate empty space.

ghost-teacup.heading: Give the white silhouette a quiet background
ghost-teacup.use: This ghost suits a lighthearted Halloween reading corner, a personal invitation, or a warm-drink themed journal page. The teacup gives the character an everyday action and helps distinguish it from a generic floating ghost. Use enough space around the cup handle and steam to preserve that small story.
ghost-teacup.edit: Keep the white body light and use the lavender folds to describe its shape. Recolor the cup for an accent, then check whether its stripes still contrast with the base. A pale blue or muted warm background can help you inspect the white edges before exporting.
ghost-teacup.check: A background chosen on this page is only a preview. To include a colored background in the file, open the editor and set it there. On very small prints, check that the cup and facial features remain distinct.

bat-crescent-flight.heading: Let the wings set the spacing
bat-crescent-flight.use: The open wings create a wide visual line inside the square canvas. Use the bat above a short heading or as a single accent on a Halloween activity sheet. Keep the moon separate from the words so it reads as part of the scene. This is a stylized character illustration, not an anatomical reference.
bat-crescent-flight.edit: Select the wing and body layers separately to experiment with a coordinated palette. Preserve a visible difference between the face and the surrounding dark shapes. If you move the moon, check the overall balance rather than simply centering every object.
bat-crescent-flight.check: The scalloped wing edges are important to recognition. A tight crop can cut off the tips, and an uneven width/height change distorts the wings. Check the full silhouette at the final document size.

spider-thread-and-bow.heading: Use the thread as a natural hanging point
spider-thread-and-bow.use: Place the spider near the top of a personal party card or Halloween worksheet so the thread has a believable starting edge. The ochre bow adds a small warm accent to the dark body. Leave space around all eight legs if the activity invites children to notice or count them.
spider-thread-and-bow.edit: Recolor the bow independently of the body. When adjusting the legs, use the Layers list to select a narrow piece instead of trying to click its line on a small screen. Keep a saved version before moving multiple pieces; their spacing helps the character remain readable.
spider-thread-and-bow.check: The thread and curved legs can disappear when reduced too far. Print one sample at the intended size and inspect these lines. The drawing is decorative and should not be presented as a scientific diagram.

apple-orchard-cutaway.heading: Keep the apple and slice in conversation
apple-orchard-cutaway.use: Use the paired fruit as an autumn notebook accent or beside a short food-related writing prompt. The red skin and cream slice create contrast without needing a large background shape. Keeping both pieces together preserves the distinction between a whole fruit and a cut view.
apple-orchard-cutaway.edit: Try changing the skin color while leaving the slice light, then adjust the highlight so it belongs to the new palette. Keep the two seed shapes distinct from the surrounding cream area. Moving the slice closer can make a compact label, but avoid overlapping it with the leaf.
apple-orchard-cutaway.check: The slice and seeds are stylized, so this artwork is not a botanical identification chart. At a small size, the seeds may merge visually; inspect a print rather than relying on an enlarged preview.

sunflower-garden-stem.heading: Build around a tall focal point
sunflower-garden-stem.use: The long stem makes this sunflower useful along the side of a personal journal page or a classroom display heading. Leave room near the two leaves and put text alongside the stem rather than across the seed center. A little empty space above the petals prevents the flower from feeling clipped.
sunflower-garden-stem.edit: The petal crown, seed details, stem, and leaves can be adjusted separately. If you simplify the seed center, retain a clear dark middle so the petals stay recognizable. Use a consistent green for related leaf and stem shapes unless a deliberate contrast improves the layout.
sunflower-garden-stem.check: Fine seed details are less important than the overall flower at small sizes. Avoid squeezing a tall arrangement into a short horizontal banner. Cropping the canvas or moving the pieces is preferable to distorting their proportions.

acorn-oak-companions.heading: Keep the woodland arrangement compact
acorn-oak-companions.use: The acorn and lobed leaf form a small cluster for an autumn reading log, nature journal decoration, or personal card. The overlapping objects give the composition depth. Leave the cap unobstructed when placing text so its scale pattern remains visible.
acorn-oak-companions.edit: The cap, shell, and leaf offer three useful color regions. Try a lighter leaf behind the dark acorn if the arrangement becomes muddy on a colored background. Keep a copy of the original positions before experimenting with a wider composition.
acorn-oak-companions.check: Small cap scales can close up on a tiny print. Check whether you need those details at all for your project. The leaf is decorative and should not be used to identify an oak species or to support a scientific claim.

gift-ribbon-keepsake.heading: Use the blank tag deliberately
gift-ribbon-keepsake.use: The blue box, cream bow, and hanging tag make a useful accent for a personal birthday card or a classroom celebration notice. The tag gives you a natural place for a very short message, but it is too small for a full sentence at typical card sizes. Keep longer wording beside the gift instead.
gift-ribbon-keepsake.edit: Change the box and ribbon colors separately, then check their contrast where the bow overlaps the lid. Use the Text tool to add a brief caption as a new layer. Moving the tag or ribbon can change their overlap, so inspect the layer order before exporting.
gift-ribbon-keepsake.check: Check the tag hole, ribbon tails, and smallest caption at final size. These are decorative elements; the exported page does not include a cut line or a template for folding a real gift box.

snowman-knitted-scarf.heading: Let the scarf carry the color
snowman-knitted-scarf.use: The snowman offers a friendly winter focal point for a personal card or seasonal classroom display. Its scarf provides the main color accent against the pale snow. Keep the arm tips and hat within the crop and use the empty area around the character for a separate message.
snowman-knitted-scarf.edit: Recolor the scarf first, then inspect any darker folds and knitted details. A pale background helps reveal the snow silhouette, but check the exported image over your destination background too. Keep facial details dark enough to remain legible on a small card.
snowman-knitted-scarf.check: A white character can lose definition on very light paper or against bright decorations. Test the outline and pale shading at actual size. A preview background does not become part of the original download unless you set it in the editor.

pumpkin-botanical-outline.heading: Keep the basket and harvest shapes readable
pumpkin-botanical-outline.use: Two pumpkins, a woven basket, an oak leaf, and a fallen acorn make a compact harvest arrangement. The open interiors suit a coloring activity or monochrome autumn journal page. Give this composition more room than a single pumpkin: the basket weave and overlapping objects need enough space to stay distinct.
pumpkin-botanical-outline.edit: Select the named pumpkin, basket, leaf, and acorn layers to simplify the arrangement. Try hiding Basket weave before increasing all line widths. A heavier stroke can close the narrow spaces between the basket and pumpkins. Put any caption outside the arrangement so it does not interrupt the coloring areas.
pumpkin-botanical-outline.check: Check the narrowest enclosed shapes in a printed proof. A complex small line drawing can be harder to color than a larger simple one. Use the actual vector PDF when printing directly; enlarging a screenshot cannot recover the original curves.
